subject: Discovery follow-up: streaming impact, p95 targets, and next-step checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Anoop Mehta <anoop@finflow.ai>, Priya Desai <priya@finflow.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:23:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery follow-up: streaming impact, p95 targets, and next-step checklist

Hi Anoop / Priya —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a short checklist so we can scope a narrow POC focused on the latency/throughput pain you described. TL;DR: we heard large p95 spikes during peak traffic, streaming UX degrades (partial token gaps), and you need predictable concurrency to support the checkout flow.

Key pain points we captured:
- Checkout autocomplete and fraud-scoring calls show p95s of ~3.2–3.8s during load tests (goal discussed: <= 800ms p95 for streaming responses).
- Streaming UX: partial-token delays cause button states to flicker in the client; users see a long pause before the last tokens arrive.
- High contention at ~300–500 concurrent model sessions; current infra falls back to CPU during spikes, multiplying tail latency.

Current stack (as told on the call):
- Model: in-house quantized Llama-13B variant served via Triton + custom batching layer
- Front-end: token-streaming over websocket to browser; simple reconnection logic
- Infra: mixed GPU pool (on-prem) + CPU fallback; no global KV cache sharing across nodes

Success criteria for the POC (proposed):
1) Streaming p95 <= 800ms for 0–2s responses and p99 < 2s for longer completions under target concurrency.
2) Sustained throughput at 300 concurrent sessions with sub-1s median latency.
3) No client-visible token gaps in streaming for sequences < 512 tokens.
4) Measurable unit-cost estimate for 1M tokens/day workload.

Immediate asks / data we need from your side:
- Representative load sample (CSV or JSON) with timestamps, payload sizes, and qps by minute (attachment stub works).
- A simple network/infra diagram showing where Triton sits, load balancers, and any NAT/gateway that could add egress latency.
- One or two sample payloads (size, tokenization) and any early termination behavior in your app.

Proposed next steps:
- You send the load sample & network diagram (this week).
- We'll scope a 2–3 week POC: initial benching + small config change (batching/kv-cache), then a short integration run on a mirrored workload.
- Schedule a 60-minute deep-dive with our infra lead (Marcus) and your SREs next Tue/Wed (Feb 24/25) — propose times: 10:00–12:00 PT.

I attached an outline we typically use for these POCs (redwood-poc-outline.pdf) and included a quick checklist below.

Jordan

jordan@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0192

Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: streaming impact, p95 targets, and next-step checklist

Jordan —

Thanks, this is great and aligned with what we need. A few clarifications / quick answers:

- Load sample: attaching a condensed minute-level CSV from Friday's simulation (finflow-load-sample.csv). You’ll see a 45-minute window where qps jumped to ~480 for 10 minutes — those are the spikes where p95s blew up.
- Network: Triton sits behind an NLB; egress passes through an internal gateway for auth. We suspect the gateway adds variable latency under load.
- Payloads: typical completion size averages 120 tokens; autocomplete requests are often single-shot (~20–40 tokens) but very sensitive to tail latency.

On success criteria: 800ms p95 is aggressive but represents the UX bar for checkout. If we can get steady numbers in the 700–900ms range with predictable tails, that will be a big win.

We're available for a deep-dive on Wed, Feb 25 at 10:30 PT — Marcus and our SRE (Ravi) will join.

Anoop
Anoop Mehta | Head of Platform, FinFlow
anoop@finflow.ai | +1 650 555 0133

Attachment: finflow-load-sample.csv (text/csv)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: streaming impact, p95 targets, and next-step checklist

Perfect — thanks for the CSV and the timing confirmation. Per Anoop's note that the NLB/gateway could be a contributor, Marcus, could you outline the bench we should run against their sample with and without the gateway in the loop? I think we should:

- Baseline: single-node perf test with identical model + token sizes (no gateway).
- Gateway-in-the-loop: run the same profile through a proxy that emulates their gateway behavior (latency, auth).
- Config experiments: continuous batching vs conservative batching; KV-cache enabled on single-node; try 8-bit quant path vs current quantization for perf/cost tradeoffs.

Marcus — can you draft a 1-page bench plan and an estimate (hours + infra) by EOD? I'll coordinate with FinFlow to get test credentials.

Also, Anoop — would you be able to upload a short trace (span IDs or correlating request IDs) for a couple of the spike windows? Even a minute-level mapping helps us isolate whether the spike is service-side model queuing or network jitter.

Jordan

Jordan / Grace / Anoop —

Draft bench plan (summary):
- Duration: 3 weeks total (1 week bench/profiling, 1 week integration runs, 1 week tuning & cost calc).
- Week 1: run baseline with their payloads on an m-simulated cluster (1 node replica -> 4 nodes) to capture queuing and KV cache behavior. Test both direct and gateway-in-loop.
- Experiments: batching window 20–200ms, KV-cache enabled/disabled, quantization variants (8-bit, 4-bit experimental path), streaming chunk size tune (64 vs 128 tokens).
- Metrics captured: latency histogram (p50/p95/p99), per-request CPU/GPU utilization, queuing delay, partial-token gaps for streaming.
- Deliverables: bench report + suggested config (ops runbook) + cost estimate for production at 1M tokens/day.

Estimate: ~24 engineer-hours (Marcus + 1 infra engineer) and ~$2,400 infra spend for a mirrored 4-node bench (can be cheaper on Reserved).

I'll put a short slide and the bench steps in the shared Drive link after this mail.

Marcus
